topic: Basics of Information Technology and Computer Science (General Science)
description: A comprehensive study guide covering the fundamental concepts of computer operations, hardware, software, memory, and the internet, optimized for the computer awareness section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Generations of Computers
sections.description: The evolutionary stages of computer development and the core technologies used in each phase.

historical_events.significance: Computers were extremely bulky, consumed vast amounts of electricity, and generated a lot of heat. Key examples include ENIAC and UNIVAC.
Replaced vacuum tubes, making computers smaller, faster, cheaper, and much more energy-efficient.
Transistors were miniaturized and placed on silicon chips (semiconductors), drastically increasing the speed and efficiency of computers.
Utilized Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) technology, bringing thousands of ICs onto a single chip, leading to the birth of Personal Computers (PCs).
Based on Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI) and parallel processing software, enabling machines to simulate human intelligence and decision-making.

sections.title: Hardware and Software
sections.description: The physical components of a computer system and the programs that drive them.

key_concepts.explanation: Hardware devices used to send data and control signals to a computer. Common examples include the Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, and Microphone.
Hardware equipment used to display or communicate the results of data processing. Common examples include Monitors, Printers, Plotters, and Speakers.
Core programs designed to run a computer's hardware and application programs. The Operating System (e.g., Windows, Linux, Android) is the most critical example.
Programs designed to perform specific tasks for the user. Examples include MS Word, web browsers, and media players.

important_facts.fact: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is known as the 'Brain of the Computer' and consists of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) and the Control Unit (CU).

sections.title: Computer Memory
sections.description: Components utilized to store data, instructions, and information within a computer system.

key_concepts.explanation: A type of volatile memory that temporarily stores data and instructions for currently running programs. Data is lost when the power is turned off.
A type of non-volatile memory that permanently stores essential system instructions, such as the BIOS needed to boot the computer.
An extremely fast, small memory located directly on or very close to the CPU, used to store frequently accessed data for rapid retrieval.

important_facts.fact: A Bit (Binary Digit 0 or 1) is the smallest unit of data in a computer. 8 Bits make 1 Byte, and 1024 Bytes equal 1 Kilobyte (KB).

sections.title: Important Keyboard Shortcuts
sections.description: Common keyboard combinations used to expedite computing tasks.

key_associations.extra_info: Saves the selected text or file to the system clipboard without removing the original.
Removes the selected item from its current location and saves it to the clipboard.
Inserts the copied or cut item from the clipboard into the current cursor location.
Reverses the last action performed by the user.
Closes the currently active window or application.

sections.title: Internet and Networking
sections.description: Systems for interconnecting computers to share resources and communicate globally.

key_concepts.explanation: A computer network that interconnects computers within a limited geographic area, such as a residence, school, or office building.
A telecommunications network that extends over a large geographic area. The Internet is the most prominent example of a WAN.
A unique numerical label assigned to every device connected to a computer network that uses the Internet Protocol for communication.

important_facts.fact: The World Wide Web (WWW) was invented by British computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.
HTTP stands for 'Hypertext Transfer Protocol', which is the foundation of data communication for the World Wide Web.
